source.prompt: What is the best CRM for a solo founder just starting out?
source.note: real collected answer; brand, competitors and publishers are the specs the cycle was scored with

answer.text:
For a solo founder just starting out, the "best" CRM isn't the one with the most enterprise features—it’s the one that is free or cheap, fast to set up, and won't distract you from building your product and talking to users.
Top options tailored to a solo founder's constraints and growth stages:
1. The Best All-in-One & Free Option: HubSpot CRM
Best for:: Founders who want marketing, sales, and customer service under one roof without paying upfront.
Why it fits: The HubSpot Free Tier offers robust contact management, deal pipelines, email tracking, meeting scheduling links, and live chat.
The Catch:: Paid tiers get expensive very quickly as you scale or need advanced automation, but as a day-one solo founder, you can stay on the free plan for a long time.
2. The Best for Pure Sales Velocity: Pipedrive
Best for:: Founders running heavy outbound sales, investor outreach, or closing high-ticket B2B deals.
Why it fits:: It’s visually driven by a Kanban board that forces you to define your next action for every single lead or prospect. Setup takes 10 minutes, and it keeps you relentlessly focused on moving relationships forward.
The Catch:: It’s a paid tool (though it offers a free trial), and it lacks a native marketing/email-blasting layer.
3. The Best Flexible & Customizable Option: Notion or Airtable
Best for:: Ultra-lean founders who already use Notion/Airtable and want a completely bespoke database.
Why it fits:: You can build a custom CRM tailored precisely to your workflow using templates, linking contacts to companies, notes, and tasks without learning dedicated CRM software.
The Catch:: No automated email tracking, native email syncing, or automated sequences out of the box—you have to do the manual logging.
4. The Best Lightweight Alternative: Close or Streak
Best for:: Gmail power users.
Why it fits:: Streak turns your actual Gmail inbox into a CRM, embedding pipeline stages directly into your email threads. It requires virtually zero context-switching.
Recommendation Summary
Go with HubSpot if you need a scalable, professional system with scheduling links and light marketing tracking for $0.
Go with Pipedrive if your primary job right now is aggressive sales outreach and closing deals.
Go with a Notion/Airtable template if you want ultimate flexibility and hate traditional software bloat.
